label_basis: Original tracked authored Rust reviewed before baseline and changed capture. Expectations use source module paths and signatures, never report-local owner ordinals.
scope: Bounded routing-only study of original repository sources already compiled by rstyle-pdg/tests/byte_call_authority.rs. Coverage of owner inventory and call edges only; no IO, purity, planner or speedup claim. This is not the full rstyle-pdg package or workspace capture.

study_routing.workspace_change: Append study package to copied workspace members. Create only the package manifest and routing-only src/lib.rs module declaration. Materialize ABSOLUTE_COPY_ROOT once before freezing the absolute-module-route copy. No original Rust source edits, wrapper functions, new dependencies or executable study behavior. Copy tracked files only, excluding untracked workspace files. Freeze each route independently for its before/after captures.
study_routing.expected_source_relation: Package-local crate root imports original oracle by absolute #[path]; original oracle and nested architecture module are outside package root and inside workspace root.
study_routing.counts_limit: Source-declared functions only; compiler-generated test harness, closures and nested generated owners are separate and must not be counted as authored coverage gains.

route_variants.purpose: Model original #[path] module integration with an absolute shared source path. Measure source-selected owner and call-edge coverage outside package root but inside explicit workspace root. Observe baseline outcomes before changed capture.

Measured nonregression control. Cargo passes target source relative to compiler cwd, so an absolute manifest target does not establish absolute #[path] module behavior. This route has no wrapper; omit runtime:: prefix for its owner labels.

baseline_observation.interpretation: Original authored owners are already known in baseline. No original-owner gain claim for this target-source route.

route_variants.purpose: Control for equivalent original shared source through dot-segment #[path] routing. Existing capture may already collect owners; measure lexical workspace-relative path and exclusion behavior, without calling retained known owners a gain.

samples.caller_signature: pub fn caller_arch(input: &[u8], n: usize) -> usize
samples.expected: Capture both original owners from the same compilation unit and retain the existing direct call edge. Missing original owners must remain unavailable, never zero-effect facts.

Capture original test function and original shared callees only in test=true context; preserve direct edges without granting strict clone admission. The ordinary library compilation must not acquire cfg(test) owners.

controls.expected: Do not merge the ordinary lib and test=true compilations, even though source files and function spellings coincide.
Compiler-generated wrappers remain distinct from authored functions and retain their existing unavailable/excluded treatment.
This study authorizes no source outside the workspace root; separate fixture acceptance must cover that boundary.
No source parsing permission or strict clone matching behavior changes are claimed.

For absolute and relative #[path] module routes, apply the same normalized workspace-relative exclusion before advisory handoff. Excluded original owners cannot become known zero-effect or complete facts. Observe baseline behavior; relative dot segments may previously bypass the glob.

capture_command_template: timeout 180 /usr/bin/time -v <binary> rstyle --manifest-path <copy>/Cargo.toml -p rstyle-shared-source-study --all-targets --format json clones --extraction-profile hir-data-v3 --compiler-advisory --compiler-plans --max-pairs 0 --locked --report-detail compact
comparison: Use the primary absolute #[path] module route for the measured owner/edge coverage comparison. For every route independently, use baseline and changed binaries/drivers on identical frozen routing, original source bytes, lockfile, selection, policy and host/toolchain. Observe baseline behavior before changed capture. Record metrics independently; do not relabel historical metric4 data. Compare source-selected owners, paths and edges in each compilation context. Module-route source labels have runtime:: prefix; target-route control omits that prefix. All changed routes should yield workspace-relative original paths and respect declared exclusions. The already measured metric4 absolute target-route has 29 known authored owner-contexts (11 lib plus 18 test), so it is a nonregression control, not a coverage gain. New routing package may require one lockfile package entry before freezing; include no dependency changes. This is coverage and policy-boundary evidence, not IO/planner or speedup evidence.
